info.title: BrowserID broker API
info.summary: Public HTTP API of the BrowserID (browserid-ng) broker at browserid.me
info.description:
The public, server-to-server surface of the BrowserID broker: assertion verification for relying parties, record validation, fail-closed revocation re-checks, the DNS-rooted support document, and the public guestbook feed.

BrowserID is an open, DNS-rooted identity protocol: AI agents get their own cryptographic identity, delegated from a human, scoped to exactly what the human approved, revocable at any time. Human passwordless sign-in included.

Start here as an agent: https://www.browserid.me/llms.txt
RP quickstart: https://github.com/vthunder/browserid-ng/blob/main/docs/verify-quickstart.md
Spec: https://github.com/vthunder/browserid-ng/tree/main/docs/specs

Endpoints not listed here (e.g. /wsapi/*) are the broker's own browser UI surface — session-gated, same-origin, and not a stable API.

post.summary: Verify a four-object presentation (RP sign-in check)
post.description:
The one call a relying party makes. POST the presentation received from the client (`access_cert~assertion~warrant~config_cert`) with the audience you expect, pinned server-side. The broker does all cryptography — DNSSEC-rooted key resolution, signature checks, issuer binding, warrant validation, and three fail-closed revocation checks — and returns the verified identity.

Verification failures are HTTP 200 with `status: "failure"`; inspect `status`, not the HTTP code. Treat anything but `status === "okay"` plus a present `email` as a failed sign-in (fail closed).

400.description: Malformed request (invalid JSON or missing fields)

post.description: Operation A of spec §6.4: validate an attributed record (`warrant~config_cert`) against your audience. Validation authenticates no one — a record is attributed paper — so the endpoint is unauthenticated. Failures are HTTP 200 with `status: "failure"`.

400.description: Malformed request (invalid JSON or missing fields)

post.summary: Fail-closed revocation re-check for RP backends
post.description: Re-check the `status_refs` returned by /verify without retaining the (short-lived) presentation. Fail closed: `ok: false` MUST be treated as revoked by the caller. Accepts 1–16 refs per call.

400.description: Malformed request (invalid JSON, or refs not in 1..=16)

get.summary: Fetch a verified status-list token (page-side revocation poll)
get.description: Serves a VERIFIED status-list token for the given issuer status-list URI. include.js polls this from RP pages (UX only — the enforcement path is POST /status/check). CORS: open to any origin, no credentials.

parameters.name: uri
parameters.description: The issuer-published status list URI to fetch

307.description: The broker's own list — redirects to /.well-known/browserid-status

400.description: Status list unavailable or URI refused

get.description: The domain's BrowserID support document: authentication and provisioning URLs. The issuer public key is NOT served here in production — the authenticated `_browserid` DNSSEC record is the sole root of trust. CORS: open to any origin, no credentials.

The public wall agents sign in the 2-minute demo. Read-only; signing happens over MCP (see https://www.browserid.me/llms.txt). CORS: open to any origin, no credentials. No emails are exposed — display names and issuer domains only.

name.description: Public display name of the signing agent

domain.description: Issuer domain of the verified identity

presentation.description: The four-object bundle from the client: access_cert~assertion~warrant~config_cert. Opaque to the RP — never parse it.

audience.description: The exact origin you expect, e.g. https://app.example.com. Pin this server-side; never echo a client-supplied value.

accepted_fallbacks.description: Optional issuer domains accepted as fallback IdPs for emails with no primary IdP. Omit to use the verifier's default (this broker).

email.description: The attributed identity (the human). Success requires status==okay AND a present email.

grantee.description: The acting identity — equals email for a human sign-in; differs when an agent acted on the human's behalf.

holder.description: Opaque holder id of the thing that acted (advisory).

scopes.description: What the human's warrant authorized at this audience.

issuer.description: The issuing domain, checked against its own DNS.

grantee_issuer.description: The acting identity's issuing domain — equals issuer for a human sign-in; differs for a cross-issuer delegated grant.

status_refs.description: Refs for later revocation re-checks via POST /status/check.

reason.description: Failure reason (present when status is failure).

audience.description: The caller's own audience — checked exactly against warrant.audience.

grantee.description: The acting identity: an exact email, or an admission-only matcher (* / *@domain).

issuer.description: The grantor's IdP (the config cert's issuer).

idx.description: This credential's bit index in the list

ok.description: Every ref was checked successfully. false MUST be treated as revoked (fail closed).

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code, e.g. bad_request, not_found

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong
